summary: This metal-plating shop released about 5,500 lb to the air in 2024, almost all zinc, and sent more to the city sewer plant.

impacts.title: Air & dust
impacts.how: About 5,500 lb of zinc compounds went into the air as fine dust and fumes, which settle nearby. Breathing zinc fumes can cause flu-like symptoms. Small amounts of nickel, a carcinogen, and chromium were also released.
avoid: Check the daily air quality index (AirNow), especially on hot, still days
Wipe dusty windowsills with a damp cloth instead of sweeping
Report strong or unusual odors to the Wisconsin DNR

impacts.title: Sewer & Lake Michigan
impacts.where: Manitowoc's wastewater plant, then Lake Michigan
impacts.how: The shop sent about 1,600 lb of nitrates plus some zinc and chromium down the sewer. The city's treatment plant removes much of this before its water reaches Lake Michigan. The exact route still needs to be confirmed.
avoid: Never pour chemicals, paint or oil down drains
Check DNR Beach Health before swimming at Manitowoc beaches
Follow the Lake Michigan fish advisory before eating your catch

impacts.title: Soil & yards
impacts.where: Homes and schoolyards near the shop
impacts.how: Metal dust that settles builds up in soil over time, where kids can swallow it while playing.
avoid: Wash kids' hands after outdoor play
Test garden soil before growing food
Take shoes off at the door
